title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 17-21): Grothendieck is axiomatising an 'analysis situs' of figures in a space X, in the spirit of the tame topology ('topologie modérée') announced in the Esquisse d'un programme. Elementary figures are now called 'multistrates'. M is the set of multistrates. It carries two order relations, X ≤ Y (X is a sub-multistrate of Y) and X << Y (X refines Y), plus a compatibility relation. A general figure is a locally finite union of mutually compatible multistrates. The 'lieux' are the multistrates that are minimal for <<. In the model case they are the points of X. L ⊂ M denotes the set of lieux.

This page introduces a 'point-set' encoding:
- For a multistrate X, L_X ⊂ L (so L_X ∈ P(L)) is the set of lieux refining X.
- \hat L_X = { L_Y | Y ≤ X } ⊂ P(L), so \hat L_X ∈ P(P(L)). It records the point-sets of all sub-multistrates of X.
- The stated aim: 'J'aimerais reconstituer les structures << et comp. sur M en termes de l'application X ↦ \hat L_X, M → P(P(L))'. In other words, recover the refinement relation and compatibility purely from these set-theoretic data.
- The same is done for a figure F ⊂ M (F ∈ P(M)):
  - L_F = set of lieux refining F = ∪_{X∈F} L_X ⊂ L;
  - \hat L_F = { L_X | X ∈ F } ∈ P(P(L)).
  This gives F ↦ \hat L_F.
- A struck attempt follows ('Soient X, Y deux multistrates. a) Supposons X << Y. Alors pour tout X_i ≤ X, soit...'). It begins proving that X << Y can be read off from these data, but is abandoned.

The next page continues:
- X_i ↦ L_{X_i} is increasing on M_{≤X}.
- One wants it strictly increasing.
- This leads to 'Cond 3': for every X, L°_X = L_X minus ∪_{X_i<X} L_{X_i} is nonempty, i.e. every multistrate has lieux 'proper' to it, like an open stratum having its own points.
- He then proves that the L°_{X_i} cover L_X.

In modern terms, this is a representation theorem in progress. An abstract poset/'site' of stratified figures, with refinement, is to be realised concretely by sets of points. Each multistrate becomes the family of point-sets of its strata (its face/closure poset), and refinement is to become a combinatorial condition on these set systems. It is analogous to recovering a space from its lattice of opens (Stone/locale 'points') and to realising a regular cell complex by its face poset.
errors: Notational: the target of X ↦ \hat L_X is written P(P(X)) (and P(P(X)) again for F ↦ \hat L_F). Given \hat L_X = {L_Y}, with L_Y ⊂ L, the target should be P(P(L)). Likely a slip of the pen, X for L.
L_F is written '∈ L' but it is a subset of L (∈ P(L)).

No result is proved on this page. The attempt to characterise << through \hat L is crossed out. Whether << and compatibility are actually determined by \hat L is left open here; it needs conditions like Cond 3 (next page).

ideas.what: Lieux (<<-minimal multistrates) as 'points' of an abstract theory of stratified figures, and encoding each multistrate X by L_X and by the set system \hat L_X = {L_Y : Y ≤ X}
ideas.modern_name: Points of an abstract stratified/tame structure; set-theoretic realisation of a face poset (cf. points of a locale, Stone representation, face posets of regular CW / stratified spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936) for the representation idea; Björner and others for face-poset realisation of regular CW complexes; o-minimal stratification theory (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5–6), but this axiomatic multistrate/lieu formalism does not appear there to my knowledge.

ideas.what: Programme to reconstruct refinement (<<) and compatibility on M from the map X ↦ \hat L_X, and the extension to figures F ↦ \hat L_F
ideas.modern_name: Representation/reconstruction of an abstract refinement poset by concrete set systems (a 'Stone duality' for stratifications)

ideas.what: (Next page) Condition that every multistrate has 'proper' lieux, L°_X ≠ ∅, making X ↦ L_X strictly monotone, with the L°_{X_i} partitioning/covering L_X
ideas.modern_name: Stratification by locally closed strata with nonempty open parts (generic points of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney/Thom stratification theory; standard in o-minimal cell decomposition

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an abstract, point-free axiomatics of tame figures (multistrates with ≤, <<, compatibility). He then tries to prove a representation theorem: the abstract refinement and compatibility relations are determined by the point-set data X ↦ {L_Y : Y ≤ X}. The attempt is abandoned on this page.
missed.quote: J'aimerais reconstituer les structures << et comp. sur M, en termes de l'application X ↦ \hat L_X M → P(P(L))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: o-minimality and tame geometry are usually set up point-set from the start (definable sets in a structure). A point-free axiomatics of stratified figures, with a recovery theorem for points, is close in spirit to locale theory and to recent 'tame' or 'pointless' approaches. Such a theory is not standard. Whether it can be completed (under conditions like Cond 3) is a concrete open question suggested by these notes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, foundational step in Grothendieck's tame-topology ('analysis situs') project: an axiomatic, point-free notion of stratified figures with a planned reconstruction of points and refinement. The page itself is mostly definitions and a programme statement, with no completed result. The general idea parallels known Stone/locale and face-poset realisation themes.
transcription_corrections: 'multistructure' should read 'multistrate' throughout (cf. p.17: 'je préfère dire maintenant multistrate').
'une des lignes qui raffinent X' should read 'ens. des lieux qui raffinent X'; likewise 'lignes' → 'lieux' elsewhere on the page.
'F ⊂ P(M)' should be 'F ∈ P(M)' (i.e. F ⊂ M).
'(ens. des lignes)' is better read as '(ens. de lieux)'.
'\mathcal L_F = ∪_{X∈F} \mathcal L_X ∈ \mathcal L' should be '⊂ \mathcal L'.
'\hat{\mathcal L}_X ⊂ \mathcal P(X)' is presumably meant as ⊂ \mathcal P(\mathcal L) (the manuscript writes X but L is intended), and the map target as P(P(L)).
Crossed-out lines near the bottom read roughly '[Pour tout X << Y]', '[Soient X, Y deux multistrates.]', '[a) Supposons X << Y. Alors pour tout X_i ≤ X, soit]'.
